real_world_materiality_existing_evidence.currently_covered_by_production: YES -- closed by merged PR #293 (part of the #293/#302/#306 slice). This is historical evidence that the pattern class is real and was costly; it is NOT a currently-uncovered incident. The frozen R2 threshold requires '1 material production incident CURRENT production predicates still miss' -- #278 fails that test on the 'currently miss' clause, even though it passes real/material/heap-proven/same-family. Treat it as REAL-WORLD MOTIVATION plus a concrete counterexample to one cheap mitigation, not as R2-satisfying materiality.
real_world_materiality_existing_evidence.pattern: boolean-parameter-guarded release, callers pass the constant that skips it -- structurally identical to guarded-consume-flag-branch/early-return, but on subscription release (-=) rather than IDisposable.Dispose()
real_world_materiality_existing_evidence.materiality: P1, heap-PROVEN via ClrMD retention-path walk on the project's own SectorTS reference codebase: 66.3% of a 223MB heap genuinely retained after 31 documents, traced to GTD.cs:5192's guarded -= (UnregisterEventHandlers(bool UnregOnlyGoodys), if (!UnregOnlyGoodys) {...}, real callers pass true)
real_world_materiality_existing_evidence.shipped_fix_mechanism: blanket/non-call-site-sensitive: 'a release guarded by a parameter of its enclosing method, outside a recognised teardown context, is NEVER credited as a release' (corpus/wpf/subscription-param-guarded-unregister). This is cheap but NOT context-sensitive -- it never had to prove itself against a safe call site that legitimately relies on the guard (the fixture's own after.cs sidesteps the guard entirely via an unconditional Dispose release rather than proving the guarded call safe).
real_world_materiality_existing_evidence.analytical_consequence: Mechanically porting that same blanket rule to the Dispose()-guarded corpus measured here would flip recall (0/4 -> 4/4) at the cost of specificity (4/4 clean -> 0/4 clean): Fine()/RunOk() call the SAME guarded method with the argument that DOES release, and the blanket rule cannot tell that call site apart from Leak()'s. This is a concrete, non-hypothetical instance of the 'traded one error class for another' failure the Dapper/Polly precision tripwires warn about -- derived from this project's own shipped code, not a synthetic argument.
real_world_materiality_existing_evidence.counter_consideration: The incident's actual shipped fix took a third path this analysis must name fairly: restructure the API so the guard disappears (move the release to an unconditional Dispose in a real teardown) rather than build a smarter checker. That is a legitimate general engineering answer to this pattern class and did not require any analyzer improvement at all.
